title: Author + implement PROP-NNN: audit why PROP-045 anti-reversion guard didn't prevent the 2026-06-03T01:27Z FUSE-revert; harden workspace-sync's universal-pusher against the dome-mirror/workspace-sync race; near-term cron-offset mitigation already applied
background:
FUSE-revert incident timeline 2026-06-03:

  01:23:55Z — `ca68cb5d` decider integrates EXP-450, closes ISS-2343/2345/2515 in its clone, pushes to git.
  01:27:00Z — `42c7e5f9` dome-mirror sentinel — should have propagated decider's commit git→FUSE.
  01:27:40Z — `42a4628b` workspace-sync pushes FUSE→git, overwriting the closures with stale FUSE content. ← ANTI-REVERSION GUARD FAILED.
  01:30:38Z — `3a709c71` integrity FAIL — caught '23 Mech-A-bypass + 2 workspace-only files, drift'. The 'drift' is the audit artifact of the revert.
  02:47:19Z — `fc9ed95c` tinker Mode 3 verified PROP-074/075 'all green' but did not catch the revert.
  03:20:11Z — `3d6d2d19` decider-2026-06-03T03-04 self-heals — detected duplicate entries (items present in both open-issues AND closed-issues) and restored ISS-2273/2275/2276/2279 to assigned-analyst where they belong post-integration. Self-healing worked but took ~2h and depended on decider noticing the drift.

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESES (tinker to validate):

  H1 — race window too narrow: workspace-sync runs at cron `0 * * * *` jitter 204s; dome-mirror runs at cron `0 * * * *` jitter 227s. Both fire in the :00-:04 window. Operator has applied a near-term mitigation 2026-06-03 ~04:55Z: moved dome-mirror to `30 * * * *` so the two agents are now ~27 min apart. This reduces race probability but does not fix the underlying anti-reversion logic.

  H2 — dome-mirror's git→FUSE sync didn't actually update FUSE's open-issues.json. Possible causes: (a) the file was excluded from the OWNERSHIP whitelist or sync-workspace step's copy list; (b) mtime-equal short-circuit kept FUSE's version; (c) cwd-resolution bug similar to PROP-074-fix-001 series; (d) workspace-sync's universal-pusher ran from a FUSE snapshot taken BEFORE dome-mirror's propagation actually landed on disk.

  H3 — PROP-045 anti-reversion guard's content-comparison logic was bypassed. Possible: (a) it compares mtime not content hash, and FUSE's mtime appeared newer; (b) it has an enforce/shadow split where this case fell in shadow; (c) the guard is keyed to specific filenames and open-issues.json isn't in its list; (d) the guard fired but its 'skip' decision was overridden somewhere downstream.

  H4 — workspace-sync's per-session FUSE was stale to begin with: workspace-sync's session FUSE may not have seen decider's commit at all by the time it ran, even though dome-mirror had finished writing to ITS session FUSE. Cross-session FUSE staleness is a known pattern.

The decider's self-heal at 03:20 is the load-bearing safety net. It works but is reactive and depends on the duplicate-detect heuristic still being correct. Tinker should treat decider's auto-heal as the canary, not the fix.

operator_decision.rationale: This bug class (FUSE↔git overwrite race) has bitten us before (the 2026-05-21 mass-delete disaster traces to the same surface area). PROP-045 was supposed to be the fix; today's incident shows the fix is incomplete or wrong for this specific race. Worth Opus-level investigation before the next overlap happens.

requested_work: Step 1 — Read monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md (full) to map the universal-pusher logic. Locate every step that writes git from FUSE. For each write path, identify the staleness check (mtime? content hash? both? neither?). Document any place where the check has an enforce/shadow split or a bypass.

Step 2 — Read monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-045-*.json (the anti-reversion guard spec) to understand what was supposed to be enforced. Compare against the workspace-sync.md implementation to find the gap.

Step 3 — Reconstruct the 01:27:40Z incident in detail. Pull the run report (monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/run-2026-06-03T0127*.json — exact path TBD by tinker). Look for skip records, anti-reversion-skips, decision logs that explain WHY workspace-sync chose to push open-issues.json despite the 4-min-prior decider commit. The smoking-gun signal will be either (a) anti-reversion guard didn't fire on open-issues.json, (b) it fired but logged 'enforce=false, shadow only', or (c) it fired and decided FUSE was newer.

Step 4 — Check the corresponding dome-mirror sentinel (monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-2026-06-03T01-27-*.json). Did it actually copy open-issues.json from git to FUSE, or was it filtered out? Look at files_copied count and the output_tail for whether open-issues.json appears.
Step 5 — Diagnose: synthesize the H1-H4 hypothesis-validation into a clear root-cause statement. Tinker may discover the actual cause is a 5th hypothesis. Document it.

Step 6 — Author monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-anti-reversion-guard-hardening.json with the diagnosis + proposed fix. Operator pre-approves the following fix directions (tinker picks the cleanest):
  (a) Switch PROP-045's anti-reversion guard from mtime-based to content-hash-based. mtime is unreliable in multi-process FUSE-vs-git setups; content equality is robust.
  (b) Add a 'recent-git-commit guard': if origin/main's HEAD timestamp on the relevant file's last touch is < N seconds old (e.g., 300s = 5 min), refuse to push FUSE→git for that file regardless of mtime/content comparison. This protects against the race window explicitly.
  (c) Enumerate decider-writeable files and short-circuit them in workspace-sync: if the file's owner-of-record per CLAUDE.md is decider (e.g., open-issues.json, closed-issues.json, closure-ledger.jsonl, expansion-tracker.json), workspace-sync NEVER pushes them — period. The universal-pusher's value was rescuing files that decider committed-but-couldn't-push due to PAT issues; that recovery path can be made conditional on a sentinel rather than always-on.
  Operator preference: (b) for simplicity and the right safety property — recent commits inherently take precedence over FUSE state.

Step 7 — Tinker self-applies the workspace-sync.md edits per the PROP-070/072/073 pattern: write proposal, implement in same run if total LOC <80 across workspace-sync.md + any monitor/scripts/ helpers, verification_pattern passes. Hold for operator review if a Q-OP needs answering or if tinker discovers the underlying race needs architectural redesign rather than guard-tweak.

Step 8 — Validate: simulate the 01:23 → 01:27 timeline. The fix should refuse to push when origin's HEAD timestamp on open-issues.json is < 5 min old. Document the simulated outcome in the PROP's verification section.
Step 9 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-NNN.json status='implemented' with commit/at/run. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set.
Step 10 — Manually copy edited workspace-sync.md to FUSE so the next workspace-sync cycle picks up the new logic.

Step 11 — Document the cron-offset change (dome-mirror moved from :00 to :30) in the PROP file's 'related mitigations' section as a near-term operator-side action. Note that the offset can be reverted to :00 once the anti-reversion guard is fixed and proven across multiple cycles.
non_goals: Do NOT change dome-mirror's git→FUSE responsibilities. PROP-074's architectural separation stands. The fix is in workspace-sync's anti-reversion logic, not dome-mirror's prompt.

Do NOT remove workspace-sync's universal-pusher mode (the rescue of decider files when decider can't push directly). That recovery path is valuable when it works — it just needs to fail safe in the race case.
Do NOT touch CLAUDE.md's OWNERSHIP table. The file classifications are correct; the bug is in the enforcement logic.
Do NOT scope to fixing ISS-2519 in this directive. That is DIRECTIVE-20260603-001 (separate, parallel).

Do NOT revert the cron-offset mitigation in this directive even if the underlying fix lands cleanly. Let the offset prove the fix is working over 2-3 days, then a separate operator decision can revert the cron back to :00.

Tinker should NOT try to merge them — they're independent fixes — but if Step 5 diagnosis surfaces a connection (e.g., the bypass IS the FUSE-revert because revert removes the verification_pattern), note it for cross-reference.

expected_output: (1) monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-anti-reversion-guard-hardening.json with status='implemented'. (2) Edit to monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md adding the recent-commit guard (preferred design (b)) or content-hash guard (design (a)) or NEVER_PUSH expansion (design (c)). (3) This directive at status='completed'. (4) FUSE-synced workspace-sync.md. (5) Validation simulation documented in PROP's verification section.
estimated_effort: ~60-90 min Opus. The diagnosis (Steps 1-5) is the longest piece (~40 min) since it requires reading several files and reconstructing the timeline. Implementation (Steps 6-8) is short (~20 min, ~30 lines). Lifecycle (Steps 9-11) is mechanical (~15 min).
priority_note: HIGH — race-condition bug class that has produced both today's revert and the May 21 mass-delete disaster on adjacent surface area. The cron-offset mitigation reduces probability but doesn't fix the bug. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs alongside DIRECTIVE-20260603-001.
